title: Admin / privileged UI
summary: Unauthenticated and member access to admin routes, verb swaps, hidden UI, impersonation, CSRF, and clickjacking.

groups.title: Who can call it
groups.summary: Admin is a function, not a hidden link.

checks.title: Unauthenticated admin routes
checks.why: /admin, /manage, or /internal answers without a session.
checks.validate: A privileged function executes with no credential.

variants.name: Common admin paths
variants.payload:
GET /admin HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: 401/302 to login, not a dashboard. Repeat /administrator/, /manage/, /internal/, /console/, /debug/.
variants.why: Predictable /admin-style paths are reachable only if a route binds them; a 200 is the finding.

variants.name: Admin host
variants.payload:
GET / HTTP/1.1
Host: admin.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: A separate admin hostname still needs authentication. A 200 app is a lead, not yet a finding.
variants.why: An admin vhost or host-routed control panel can be discovered through DNS and host headers.

checks.title: Member token on admin functions
checks.why: Admin routes exist in the spec or the JS bundle, and a member session can call them.
checks.validate: A privileged function executes for a caller the matrix denies.

variants.name: Member session on /admin
variants.payload:
GET /admin/users HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<member>
variants.expect: 403/404, not a user list. Repeat /api/v1/admin/users and actions you saw in the bundle.
variants.why: A member token reaching an admin function is a function-level authorization gap.

variants.name: Hidden UI is not a control
variants.payload:
POST /admin/users/42/role HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<member>
Content-Type: application/json

{"role":"admin"}
variants.expect: If the button is hidden but the route works, that is BFLA.
variants.why: A route hidden from the menu is still reachable if it has no server-side check.

variants.name: Version and alias
variants.payload:
GET /api/v0/admin/users HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
variants.expect: Older versions, trailing slashes, and case variants.
variants.why: Versioned or aliased admin routes can bypass a path allowlist that matches only the canonical URL.

checks.title: Verb and method override
checks.why: GET is allowed and DELETE is not — unless a method override reaches DELETE.
checks.validate: A member performs an admin mutation through an alternate verb.

variants.name: DELETE as member
variants.payload:
DELETE /api/v1/users/42 HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
variants.expect: 403, not a deleted user. Also PUT, PATCH, OPTIONS.
variants.why: A member changing the effective verb to a destructive one on an admin object is the finding.

variants.name: X-HTTP-Method-Override
variants.payload:
POST /api/v1/users/42 HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
X-HTTP-Method-Override: DELETE
Content-Length: 0
variants.expect: Override must not reach a handler the real DELETE would refuse. Also try _method=DELETE.
variants.why: A header override lets a read-like request become a destructive verb the route would otherwise deny.

checks.title: Impersonation / support access
checks.why: A support or admin impersonation action is callable by a member, or does not leave an audit trail.
checks.validate: A becomes B without being an eligible admin, or the action is not attributed.

variants.name: Member impersonate
variants.payload:
POST /admin/users/1002/impersonate HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<member>
variants.expect: Must 403. Repeat /sudo, /act-as, /login-as.
variants.why: A non-privileged account requesting impersonation is a privilege escalation.

variants.name: Admin impersonate without step-up
variants.payload: As a real admin, impersonate your other test user and look for re-auth and an audit event.
variants.expect: Missing step-up or a missing audit row is the finding — do not impersonate a real customer.
variants.why: Impersonating another admin without re-authentication skips the intended step-up control.

groups.title: CSRF and framing
groups.summary: Admin mutations are the highest-value CSRF and clickjacking targets.

checks.title: CSRF on admin actions
checks.why: A cross-site POST creates a user, changes a role, or issues a refund.
checks.validate: A cross-origin form changes admin state in the victim admin session.

variants.name: Cross-site role change
variants.payload:
<form action="https://www.example.com/admin/users/42/role" method="POST">
  <input name="role" value="admin">
</form>
<script>document.forms[0].submit()</script>
variants.expect: Must fail without a valid CSRF token. Critical actions should also require step-up.
variants.why: A cross-site POST that changes roles is a high-impact CSRF on a privileged action.

variants.name: JSON as text/plain
variants.payload:
POST /api/v1/admin/users HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Content-Type: text/plain
Origin: https://evil.example
Cookie: session=<admin>

{"email":"attacker@example.com","role":"admin"}
variants.expect: Must not create a user.
variants.why: Simple-request JSON must still carry a token or it can be CSRF'd cross-site.

checks.title: Clickjacking the admin UI
checks.why: A third-party page can frame /admin and steal a click on a destructive control.
checks.validate: A cross-origin iframe of the admin page either fails to load or there is no sensitive control.

variants.name: Read framing headers
variants.payload:
GET /admin HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<admin>
variants.expect: frame-ancestors 'none' or an explicit allowlist. XFO DENY/SAMEORIGIN must not contradict CSP.
variants.why: The framing policy is read before any frame test so the expectation is grounded.

variants.name: Cross-origin iframe
variants.payload:
<!doctype html>
<iframe src="https://www.example.com/admin" style="width:100%;height:100%"></iframe>
variants.expect: The iframe stays blank / errors when framing is denied.
variants.why: An actual frame load confirms whether the admin UI can be clickjacked.

checks.title: Build and verify the role-permission matrix
checks.why: Every later authorization test needs a written map of who can do what — otherwise findings are anecdotes, not coverage.
checks.validate: A matrix of roles x functions x objects (including tenant dimensions) that the engagement tests against.

variants.name: Documented matrix
variants.payload: From documentation, UI walkthroughs as each test account, and owner confirmation, write the matrix: role, functions reachable, object scopes, tenant reach.
variants.expect: Matrix reviewed by the owner as intended behaviour — it becomes the oracle for every gap test.
variants.why: The oracle comes first; findings are deviations from it.

variants.name: UI reach sweep
variants.payload: Walk every role account through the app; record reachable functions and object types per role.
variants.expect: Observed reach matches the matrix; extra reach becomes a finding, missing reach becomes a question.
variants.why: The UI is the cheapest complete function inventory.

variants.name: API surface overlay
variants.payload: Repeat the sweep at the API layer (routes the UI uses plus documented endpoints).
variants.expect: API reach per role matches UI reach per role; unexplained differences are test targets.
variants.why: UI hiding what the API allows is the classic split.

checks.title: Horizontal delete authorization
checks.why: Destructive operations get the least casual testing and cause the most damage when authorization is missing.
checks.validate: DELETE (and destructive POST/PUT) on another user object is refused with 403/404, and nothing is soft-deleted.

variants.name: Swap the path id
variants.payload:
DELETE /api/objects/1002 HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Cookie: session=<account-A> — 1002 belongs to test account B (yours).
variants.expect: 403/404 for B id; only A-owned ids delete. Confirm with B that 1002 still exists.
variants.why: Direct cross-account delete with your own two accounts.

variants.name: Soft-delete parity
variants.payload: Repeat with destructive verbs and shapes: POST /objects/1002/delete, PUT {deleted:true}, POST /trash with the id in body.
variants.expect: Every destructive shape enforces ownership — route-level checks miss body-borne ids.
variants.why: One guarded verb and three unguarded twins is a common pattern.

variants.name: Bulk delete smuggling
variants.payload: Include B id inside a batch you legitimately own: DELETE ids=[1001(own),1002(B)].
variants.expect: Whole request rejected or per-member partial refuse — never silently delete the foreign member.
variants.why: Bulk endpoints must authorize per member, not per request.

checks.title: Collections filtered by caller permissions
checks.why: List endpoints leak other users data without any id guessing — the response simply contains it.
checks.validate: Every collection response contains only objects the caller may read; totals and pagination respect the same filter.

variants.name: Own-list baseline
variants.payload: GET /api/objects as account A: note count and a stable marker field.
variants.expect: Only A-owned (or A-visible) objects return; record the shape for cross-account comparison.
variants.why: Establish what correct looks like first.

variants.name: Foreign-object presence
variants.payload: Create an object as B with a canary title; list as A (default list, search, sort, filters).
variants.expect: B canary never appears in any A listing — including exports, suggestions, and typeaheads.
variants.why: Auxiliary list shapes (typeahead, recent, suggested) are where filters are forgotten.

variants.name: Pagination and totals
variants.payload: Compare reported totals/pagination metadata with the filtered content length as A.
variants.expect: Totals count only A-visible objects; unfiltered counts leak existence and volume.
variants.why: Metadata is data too.

checks.title: Bulk operations authorize per member
checks.why: Batch endpoints authorize the request once and apply it to every member — one foreign id inside a batch is a multiplier.
checks.validate: Each member of a batch is authorized individually; foreign members fail without partial application of side effects.

variants.name: Mixed batch
variants.payload: POST /api/objects/batch-update ids=[A-own, B-foreign] with a harmless field change.
variants.expect: Rejected (all-or-nothing) or per-member partial with B refused — never B applied.
variants.why: The minimal honest batch probe with two of your own objects.

variants.name: All-foreign batch
variants.payload: A batch containing only B ids under A session.
variants.expect: Complete refusal; no metadata leakage about B object existence beyond a flat deny.
variants.why: Response detail here is also an existence oracle (see separate check).

variants.name: Nested batch shapes
variants.payload: Repeat via every batch transport the app uses: array body, CSV import, patch-document arrays, GraphQL lists.
variants.expect: Same per-member enforcement across transports.
variants.why: Enforcement often exists on one path only.

checks.title: Parent-child authorization on nested routes
checks.why: GET /own/child is guarded, but /parents/<other>/children/<own> style nesting lets idor hide in the middle segment.
checks.validate: Authorization is evaluated on the full path chain: every ancestor must belong to (or be reachable by) the caller.

variants.name: Foreign parent, own child
variants.payload: GET /api/users/<B>/orders/<A-order-id> as A — your order under the other account path.
variants.expect: 403/404: the parent check must fail even though the child is yours.
variants.why: Child-ownership checks are not ancestor checks.

variants.name: Foreign child, own parent
variants.payload: GET /api/users/<A>/orders/<B-order-id>.
variants.expect: 403/404 — middle segments are authorization inputs everywhere.
variants.why: The mirror case catches inverse-only validation.

variants.name: Deep chain walk
variants.payload: Build the deepest documented route (4+ segments) and swap the least-checked middle segment.
variants.expect: Swap rejected; record which segment levels lack checks for the report.
variants.why: Longer chains accumulate unvalidated segments.

checks.title: Opaque references treated as inputs, not secrets
checks.why: UUIDs and opaque handles delay guessing, but they are not authorization — a leaked or shared reference must still deny.
checks.validate: Access decisions run on ownership/permission for every reference format, not on the unguessability of the id.

variants.name: Handle handoff
variants.payload: Copy the full reference (UUID, hash, ref token) of a B object from a legitimate B-side view you control; request it as A.
variants.expect: 403/404 — knowing the reference grants nothing.
variants.why: The honest test: full knowledge of the identifier, still denied.

variants.name: Sequential-vs-opaque mix
variants.payload: Find endpoints that accept both sequential and opaque forms of the same object; try the sequential form where the UI uses opaque.
variants.expect: Same enforcement regardless of representation.
variants.why: Alternate representations are alternate entrances.

variants.name: Cross-format objects
variants.payload: Use a document ref where a message id is expected (and similar type confusions across namespaces).
variants.expect: Type/scope mismatch rejected — references are namespace-bound.
variants.why: Global uniqueness without scoping invites cross-type confusion.

checks.title: Direct file and media retrieval authorized
checks.why: Uploads, avatars, and exports are often served from a storage path with no per-object decision — the URL is the only lock.
checks.validate: Fetching any file object requires an authorized session decision per object, including direct storage URLs.

variants.name: B media as A
variants.payload: As B upload a canary file; take its direct URL (CDN or app path); fetch it as A and in a private window (unauthenticated).
variants.expect: 403/404 (or signed-URL refusal) both ways — private media stays private even with the URL.
variants.why: URL-knowledge is the attacker model for leaked links.

variants.name: Signed-URL scope
variants.payload: Where signed URLs exist: take B signed URL, strip/alter signature and query params, try as A.
variants.expect: Altered signatures fail; signatures are bound to object and expiry (see signed-URL check for depth).
variants.why: Signature tamper-proving before deeper scope tests.

variants.name: Listing paths
variants.payload: Request the directory/listing endpoints or predictable adjacent names (file-1.jpg..file-3.jpg) around A-owned media.
variants.expect: No enumeration of sibling or foreign objects.
variants.why: Adjacent guessing costs nothing to test.

checks.title: Reports and export artifacts authorized
checks.why: Generated reports aggregate data the UI protects — the artifact often sits on a less-guarded download path.
checks.validate: Downloading any generated artifact requires caller ownership/permission at download time, not just at generation time.

variants.name: B report as A
variants.payload: As B generate an export/report; capture its download URL or id; fetch as A.
variants.expect: 403/404 — artifact ids are authorization-bound.
variants.why: Generation-time checks without download-time checks.

variants.name: Post-revocation download
variants.payload: Generate as A, have permissions revoked (owner-assisted), then download.
variants.expect: Download refused — artifact access follows current permission, not a snapshot.
variants.why: Exports outlive the sessions that made them.

variants.name: Guessable artifact ids
variants.payload: If artifact ids look sequential/timestamped, probe adjacent values for your own artifacts only.
variants.expect: Adjacent fetches fail or return only A artifacts; report enumerability evidence without touching foreign data.
variants.why: Stay on your own objects while proving the pattern.

checks.title: Async jobs authorized end to end
checks.why: Queued work runs with worker authority — status, cancellation, and result endpoints are the user-facing doors to it.
checks.validate: Job status, cancellation, and results all check the caller against the job owner at request time.

variants.name: B job status as A
variants.payload: As B start a long job (export, import, report); poll its status endpoint as A with the job id.
variants.expect: 403/404 — status is authorization data too (progress, payload names).
variants.why: Status endpoints leak and control.

variants.name: Cancel foreign job
variants.payload: POST cancel on the B job id as A.
variants.expect: Refused — cancelling other people work is integrity, not just confidentiality.
variants.why: Cancellation is a destructive operation.

variants.name: Results after permission change
variants.payload: Complete a job as A, lose the underlying permission (owner-assisted), fetch results.
variants.expect: Results refused — job outputs inherit current authority over the source data.
variants.why: Workers remember; endpoints must re-check.

checks.title: Hidden UI is not authorization
checks.why: Buttons hidden per role stop honest users; the API behind them serves anyone who asks.
checks.validate: Every function reachable through the UI is enforced server-side per role, independent of what the UI renders.

variants.name: Hidden-button API call
variants.payload: As a limited role, find functions the UI hides; drive their API calls directly (Repeater).
variants.expect: 403 — server-side role enforcement, evidenced per endpoint.
variants.why: The canonical client-side authorization test.

variants.name: Disabled-field payload
variants.payload: Re-enable a disabled field in DevTools, submit, and watch the request.
variants.expect: Server decides with its own permission model; tampered clients change nothing.
variants.why: Cheapest tamper that proves the point.

variants.name: Route-direct navigation
variants.payload: Navigate directly to hidden routes (URL/SPA state) as the limited role.
variants.expect: Route guards server-side; UI routing is convenience.
variants.why: Deep links bypass menus, never enforcement.

checks.title: Ownership cannot be reassigned by client fields
checks.why: Mass assignment on owner/user/tenant fields transfers objects (or grants access) with one crafted update.
checks.validate: Server-controlled fields (owner, roles, tenant, pricing tier, flags) are ignored or rejected in client payloads.

variants.name: Owner field overwrite
variants.payload: PUT /api/objects/1001 (A-owned) with {"owner_id": <B-test-id>} added to the normal payload.
variants.expect: Field ignored or 400 — ownership never changes from client input.
variants.why: The classic mass-assignment probe on the most dangerous field.

variants.name: Role/tier bump
variants.payload: POST registration or PUT profile including role=admin, tier=premium, is_admin=true variants.
variants.expect: Ignored/rejected; registration and profile flows assign only default roles.
variants.why: Self-service endpoints must not mint privilege.

variants.name: Transfer flow abuse
variants.payload: If a legitimate transfer/invite flow exists, complete it with yourself then attempt to skip its confirmation step via direct state changes.
variants.expect: Transfers honor their full workflow; state cannot be jumped by field edits.
variants.why: Legitimate flows abused are worse than absent ones.

checks.title: Sensitive properties filtered by read permission
checks.why: Field-level data (tokens, internal notes, cost price, PII) often rides along in objects the caller may otherwise read.
checks.validate: Responses include sensitive fields only for roles/contexts with that field-level permission.

variants.name: Field diff across roles
variants.payload: Fetch the same object type as two roles you hold; diff the response keys.
variants.expect: Sensitive keys absent for the lesser role — not null-empty but absent (or explicitly permitted).
variants.why: A clean structural diff beats reading values.

variants.name: Alternate representations
variants.payload: Repeat the diff across representations: ?fields=*, export CSV, mobile API, and internal fields in errors.
variants.expect: Every representation applies the same field rules.
variants.why: Exports and mobile shapes forget filters.

variants.name: Nested/embedded copy
variants.payload: Check the same fields when the object is embedded in a parent response (/me containing full account object).
variants.expect: Embedded copies follow the same field permission as direct reads.
variants.why: Embedding re-serializes and re-leaks.

checks.title: Protected properties reject unauthorized writes
checks.why: Readable-but-not-writable fields (balance, status, limits, audit fields) must refuse edits from roles without that write permission.
checks.validate: Writes to protected properties are rejected for unauthorized roles, with no partial application.

variants.name: Balance/status edit
variants.payload: PUT the object as the lesser role with {"balance":999999} or {"status":"approved"} included.
variants.expect: Rejected or ignored with the rest of the update applied per policy — protected fields never change.
variants.why: One payload, two field classes: normal and protected.

variants.name: Deep-merge reach
variants.payload: Send nested paths to protected fields (settings.tier, meta.flags.admin).
variants.expect: Deep merges do not tunnel into protected branches.
variants.why: Frameworks that merge deep give writers long arms.

variants.name: Write-via-read-representation
variants.payload: Round-trip: GET the object, modify the protected field in the copy, PUT it back.
variants.expect: The read representation is not a writable contract — protected fields still refuse.
variants.why: Editable-looking JSON is not a permission.

checks.title: Authorization rechecked when object state changes
checks.why: Approved-then-locked, published-then-restricted: permissions depend on state, and stale checks keep old access alive.
checks.validate: State transitions that change reachability re-evaluate authorization for in-flight and follow-up access.

variants.name: Lock-then-read
variants.payload: Owner-assisted: move your test object into a restricted state (lock, unpublish, close); immediately re-read and re-edit as before.
variants.expect: New state enforced on the next request — no grace access to restricted states.
variants.why: The check must follow the object, not the session.

variants.name: Transition race
variants.payload: Submit a state-changing action, and mid-flight (before completion) fire the follow-up action that the new state should block.
variants.expect: Follow-up evaluated against current state at execution time — TOCTOU closed.
variants.why: State machines are authorization machines with extra steps.

variants.name: Workflow-boundary edit
variants.payload: After an object enters approval/review, attempt direct edits as the original owner.
variants.expect: Owner edits blocked per workflow rules; review states are integrity states.
variants.why: Owner is a role that state can narrow.

checks.title: Authorization independent of display attributes
checks.why: Theme, locale, feature-flag, and layout fields sometimes double as authority — if the server reads them for decisions, users mint permissions.
checks.validate: No authorization decision reads user-controllable display/preference attributes.

variants.name: Preference-field sweep
variants.payload: List preference-ish fields (theme, locale, plan display, dashboard config, feature flags in profile).
variants.expect: None of these appear in access decisions — verified by role-matrix diff, not assumption.
variants.why: Inventory before inference.

variants.name: Flag flip probe
variants.payload: Flip profile-carried feature flags (feature_x_enabled=true) via their normal settings endpoints; probe gated functions.
variants.expect: Gating is server-permission based; flag changes do not unlock.
variants.why: Client flags steer UI; server flags steer access.

variants.name: Config-injection shapes
variants.payload: Send dashboard/config blobs containing role- or permission-looking keys.
variants.expect: Unknown keys ignored; blobs are data, never policy.
variants.why: Flexible config fields attract policy smuggling.

checks.title: Error, preview, and metadata representations authorized
checks.why: Validation errors, preview renders, audit metadata, and schema endpoints re-serialize objects — filters are easily forgotten there.
checks.validate: Every representation of an object (errors, previews, metadata, docs) enforces the same read permissions as the primary view.

variants.name: Error-message reflection
variants.payload: Request B object as A with malformed payloads that echo object content in validation errors.
variants.expect: Errors carry no B field values — error paths serialize too.
variants.why: Error messages are representations.

variants.name: Preview render
variants.payload: Use preview/preview-link features on B object ids as A.
variants.expect: Preview refuses or renders only A-visible content.
variants.why: Previews bypass the detail page, so they skip its guards.

variants.name: Metadata/schema leak
variants.payload: Fetch schema/options/metadata endpoints for B ids (field definitions, owners, timestamps).
variants.expect: Metadata follows the same visibility as the data it describes.
variants.why: Metadata is half the story in reports.

checks.title: Audit events without leaking protected data
checks.why: Audit logs prove authorization decisions — but the logs themselves become a data leak if user-facing views expose protected content.
checks.validate: User-visible audit/log views redact protected data and enforce viewer permissions on event payloads.

variants.name: Audit view sweep
variants.payload: Open user-facing activity/log views as A; inspect events for other users content, tokens, or full payloads.
variants.expect: Events describe actions, not payloads; cross-user events only where intended.
variants.why: Logs written for auditors, shown to users, leak both ways.

variants.name: Event injection
variants.payload: Cause log-worthy actions containing canary strings (display-name canary) as B; view logs as A.
variants.expect: Canary does not surface to A through any log or event surface.
variants.why: Proves payload propagation end to end.

variants.name: Immutability poke
variants.payload: Attempt to edit/delete own audit events via any user-reachable path.
variants.expect: Audit events are append-only for users; no deletion or edit path exists.
variants.why: Editable audit logs are not audit logs.

checks.title: Tenant context bound to trusted identity
checks.why: Tenant chosen from request input (header, subdomain, form field) lets any authenticated user shop tenants.
checks.validate: Tenant context derives from verified identity claims (token/session) only; request-borne tenant values are ignored.

variants.name: Header/param override
variants.payload: With A-in-tenant-1 session, replay requests with X-Tenant: 2, tenant_id=2 body field, and ?tenant=2 variants.
variants.expect: Tenant stays 1 — every transport ignored.
variants.why: Enumerate transports; one accepted is the bypass.

variants.name: Subdomain hop
variants.payload: If tenants map to subdomains, take the tenant-1 session cookie to the tenant-2 subdomain.
variants.expect: Rejected — session is tenant-bound (cookie scope + server binding).
variants.why: Subdomain front doors need server-side tenant binding behind them.

variants.name: Token-tenant mismatch
variants.payload: Craft (with app-owned test keys) or obtain a token whose tenant claim differs from the request context.
variants.expect: Server resolves tenant from the authoritative claim chain with defined precedence, never from the lesser source.
variants.why: Ambiguity between two tenant signals is the flaw.

checks.title: Cross-tenant object access refused
checks.why: Object-level checks that verify user but not tenant leak data across the strongest boundary in the product.
checks.validate: Every object access checks tenant membership in addition to ownership/permission.

variants.name: Foreign-tenant object id
variants.payload: With two test tenants you hold: request tenant-2 object ids from a tenant-1 session (path, body, and alternate representations).
variants.expect: 403/404 everywhere — tenant is part of every object predicate.
variants.why: The core boundary test with your own two tenants.

variants.name: Search/lookup leak
variants.payload: Search tenant-1 for canary content created in tenant-2.
variants.expect: No cross-tenant hits in search, suggestions, or recent lists.
variants.why: Search indexes often span tenants by accident.

variants.name: Reference across tenants
variants.payload: Link, share, or attach tenant-2 objects into tenant-1 containers.
variants.expect: Cross-tenant references rejected at create and at render.
variants.why: Relations are object access too.

checks.title: Tenant switch clears object and permission state
checks.why: Switching tenants mid-session with cached lists, permissions, or single-page state bleeds one tenant context into another.
checks.validate: Tenant switch re-establishes context atomically: lists, permissions, drafts, and uploads from the old tenant do not survive.

variants.name: Canary carry-over
variants.payload: Load tenant-1 lists/drafts in the UI; switch to tenant-2; watch network and UI for tenant-1 content.
variants.expect: Fresh tenant-2 state only; no tenant-1 requests or remnants.
variants.why: The user-visible version of the boundary.

variants.name: Parallel-tab switch
variants.payload: Keep tenant-1 open in one tab while switching to tenant-2 in another; act in the old tab.
variants.expect: Old tab re-authorizes per request and fails closed against the new session state.
variants.why: Stale tabs are the real multi-tenant client.

variants.name: Switch mid-flow
variants.payload: Start a multi-step flow (wizard, upload) in tenant-1, switch tenants, complete the flow.
variants.expect: Flow either restarts or carries with explicit tenant re-validation — never silently lands in the wrong tenant.
variants.why: Multi-step flows cache early context.

checks.title: Tenant invitations and role assignment authorized
checks.why: Invite and role-assign endpoints create members and privileges — weak checks here mint admins.
checks.validate: Only tenant-authorized roles may invite/assign; invite links are tenant- and role-bound, single-use, and expiry-limited.

variants.name: Self-elevation via invite
variants.payload: As a standard member, call the invite/assign endpoint granting yourself (or a second account you hold) an admin role.
variants.expect: Refused — role grants require the tenant privilege you lack.
variants.why: The privilege-minting probe, done to your own account.

variants.name: Cross-tenant invite
variants.payload: Invite an address into tenant-2 from tenant-1 membership (and accept from your tenant-2-capable account).
variants.expect: Invitations are tenant-scoped; cross-tenant invites rejected or land only in the inviting tenant.
variants.why: Invites are tenant membership documents.

variants.name: Invite link reuse
variants.payload: Use a valid invite link twice (second time from a different account you hold); try after expiry and after acceptance.
variants.expect: Single-use within expiry; reuse and replay refused.
variants.why: Invite links are bearer credentials with a job.

checks.title: Group and team membership changes authorized
checks.why: Membership is permission: adding yourself to a privileged group is a privilege escalation with a friendly UI.
checks.validate: Membership add/remove/role-in-group changes require the documented group authority; self-service is limited to allowed cases.

variants.name: Self-add to privileged group
variants.payload: As a standard account, call the group-membership endpoint to add yourself to an admin/privileged group.
variants.expect: Refused and logged; only authorized group managers can add.
variants.why: One request, one escalation path.

variants.name: Role-in-group bump
variants.payload: Where groups have per-member roles (owner/manager/member), promote your own membership to manager/owner.
variants.expect: Refused — per-member role changes need the level above.
variants.why: Nested privilege needs nested checks.

variants.name: Remove-your-manager
variants.payload: Attempt to remove a group owner/manager as a member, or to remove the last owner.
variants.expect: Refused; group integrity rules (last owner, manager set) enforced server-side.
variants.why: Destructive group ops have integrity guards too.

checks.title: Delegated and shared access keep scope and expiry
checks.why: Share links, delegates, and API keys outlive their intent when scope/expiry are advisory — they become permanent second identities.
checks.validate: Delegated credentials carry enforced scope and expiry; renewal cannot widen either; revocation is immediate.

variants.name: Scope fence
variants.payload: Create a share/delegate with read-only scope; attempt writes through it.
variants.expect: Writes refused — scope is enforced at execution, not recorded as metadata.
variants.why: Read-only that writes is the finding.

variants.name: Expiry reality
variants.payload: Create the shortest-lived share available; use it after expiry.
variants.expect: Refused at expiry — client-side countdowns do not count.
variants.why: Expiry is a server decision.

variants.name: Revoke-and-replay
variants.payload: Revoke the share/key; immediately replay it.
variants.expect: Dead immediately; no propagation gap beyond the documented window.
variants.why: Revocation is the user-side kill switch.

checks.title: Every workflow transition authorized
checks.why: State machines encode who may move a case from state to state — skipped checks let anyone approve, publish, or close.
checks.validate: Each transition is authorized for the current state and actor role; terminal and approval states are specially guarded.

variants.name: Forbidden transition map
variants.payload: From your test object current state, attempt every other transition the API exposes (approve as non-approver, close as requester, reopen as auditor).
variants.expect: Only role-legal transitions succeed; map accepted/rejected for the report.
variants.why: Exhaustive per state beats sampling.

variants.name: Skip-ahead
variants.payload: Fire a late-state transition (publish, payout) directly on a fresh object still in early state.
variants.expect: Rejected — order is part of authorization.
variants.why: Jumping states skips the checks between them.

variants.name: Idempotent replay
variants.payload: Replay an already-applied transition (approve twice, cancel after completion).
variants.expect: Idempotent refusal or defined re-submission — never double side effects.
variants.why: Replay semantics are authorization semantics.

checks.title: Separation of duties on approvals
checks.why: If the requester can approve their own request (or pick their approver), approval theatre replaces control.
checks.validate: Approver must differ from requester, be eligible for the object, and cannot be delegated to the requester.

variants.name: Self-approval
variants.payload: Submit a request as A; call the approve endpoint for it as A.
variants.expect: Refused — maker and checker are different identities server-side.
variants.why: The direct SoD probe.

variants.name: Approver choice
variants.payload: Where requesters nominate an approver, nominate your own second account or an ineligible role.
variants.expect: Eligibility enforced server-side; self-nomination refused.
variants.why: Attacker-chosen approvers are rubber stamps.

variants.name: Post-assignment swap
variants.payload: After legitimate assignment, attempt to reassign the approver to yourself mid-flight.
variants.expect: Reassignment follows its own authority; mid-flight swaps audited and restricted.
variants.why: The swap is the subtle escalation.

checks.title: Role revocation beats stale caches
checks.why: Permissions removed but cached (session, token, gateway, front-end) keep working — revocation with a lag is escalation with a timer.
checks.validate: Role/permission removal takes effect within the documented window on every layer that decides access.

variants.name: Revoke-then-use
variants.payload: Owner-assisted: remove a role from your test account mid-session; immediately probe role-gated endpoints.
variants.expect: Refused within the documented cache window; measure and record the window.
variants.why: The incident-response question: how fast does no mean no?

variants.name: Layer sweep
variants.payload: Repeat the probe across layers: existing session, fresh token, different endpoint families, background jobs.
variants.expect: Every deciding layer honors the revocation within the window.
variants.why: One cache forgotten keeps the door open.

variants.name: Cache-window honesty
variants.payload: Compare measured behavior against the documented SLA.
variants.expect: Measured within documented; otherwise a finding with timings.
variants.why: Windows are fine; undocumented windows are not.

checks.title: Stale self-contained role claims rejected
checks.why: JWT-bearing roles outlive revocation by design — until a role change, the old token still says admin.
checks.validate: Privilege-sensitive actions re-validate roles (short token lifetimes, server-side role checks, or token refresh on change).

variants.name: Old-token replay
variants.payload: Capture a token for your account; owner-assisted role removal; replay the token on sensitive functions.
variants.expect: Sensitive functions refuse — either token lifetime is short or the check is server-side.
variants.why: The token says who you were.

variants.name: Refresh widens nothing
variants.payload: After role removal, refresh the token and inspect its role claims.
variants.expect: Refreshed token carries current roles — no echo of old claims.
variants.why: Refresh is a re-authorization moment.

variants.name: Sensitive-function short clock
variants.payload: Record where stale-role windows are acceptable (read-only menus) vs refused (admin functions).
variants.expect: Tiered enforcement documented; high-impact functions have the shortest stale window.
variants.why: Risk-proportional staleness is a policy, not an accident.

checks.title: Each operation in batched requests authorized
checks.why: GraphQL batching, arrays, and multiplexed transports decide once per request — per-operation decisions are the fix.
checks.validate: Every operation inside a batch/multiplexed frame is authorized as if sent alone.

variants.name: Mixed batch
variants.payload: In one request batch: an allowed operation plus a forbidden one (cross-account object) as the same user.
variants.expect: The forbidden member fails alone; the allowed one proceeds per policy — never all-pass.
variants.why: Batch-level checks launder forbidden members.

variants.name: Same-object repetition
variants.payload: Repeat the same forbidden operation N times inside one batch (small N).
variants.expect: Same refusal; repetition does not wear down the check.
variants.why: Also a rate-limit observation, honestly labelled.

variants.name: Nested aliases
variants.payload: Use aliases/nested selection (GraphQL) to reach the forbidden object inside one operation.
variants.expect: Field-level authorization still applies — nesting is not anonymity.
variants.why: Aliasing hides operations from naive logging too.

checks.title: Avoid authorization existence oracles
checks.why: 404-vs-403 differences, timing gaps, and error text reveal whether objects exist — where concealment is required, that is disclosure.
checks.validate: Where concealment is a requirement, unauthorized access returns a uniform response (status, timing, error shape) regardless of existence.

variants.name: Status-code diff
variants.payload: Request existing-foreign vs nonexistent ids with the same shape and compare status codes and bodies.
variants.expect: Identical denial responses where concealment matters; document the oracle otherwise.
variants.why: Measure before demanding uniformity.

variants.name: Timing diff
variants.payload: Time both cases over a small sample; look for systematic gaps (db hits, late checks).
variants.expect: Timing consistent within noise; report measured deltas.
variants.why: Late authorization shows up as late milliseconds.

variants.name: Error-text echo
variants.payload: Compare error messages and ids echoed back for both cases.
variants.expect: No existence-revealing detail in denials.
variants.why: Friendly errors are often honest to a fault.

checks.title: Signed object URLs scoped and revocable
checks.why: A signed URL is a bearer credential for one object — unscoped signatures or long horizons leak data via link sharing.
checks.validate: Signatures bind to object, action, and short expiry; revocation invalidates outstanding URLs; scope cannot be edited.

variants.name: Signature surgery
variants.payload: Take a signed URL for A-object; alter the object path/id in it, keep the signature; fetch.
variants.expect: Fails — signature covers the exact object and method.
variants.why: The most common signed-URL flaw.

variants.name: Cross-object swap
variants.payload: Sign two of your own URLs; mix signature from one with path from the other.
variants.expect: Rejected; no signature reuse across objects.
variants.why: Two honest URLs, one dishonest combination.

variants.name: Expiry and revoke
variants.payload: Use the shortest-expiry URL after expiry; then revoke a live one and replay.
variants.expect: Both refused; expiry enforced, revocation immediate.
variants.why: Time and kill-switch on the same credential.

checks.title: Realtime channels authorized per subscription and message
checks.why: WebSockets authenticate once at handshake — subscription and per-message authorization are where channels leak.
checks.validate: Each subscribe targets channels the caller may read; each incoming message is authorized per target before relay.

variants.name: Foreign subscription
variants.payload: Over your authed socket, subscribe to a B-user or foreign-room channel/topic.
variants.expect: Subscription refused; no frames ever arrive for it.
variants.why: Handshake auth is not channel auth.

variants.name: Mid-stream revocation
variants.payload: Owner-assisted: revoke the account/socket mid-connection; observe frames.
variants.expect: Connection closed or frames stop within the documented window.
variants.why: Dead accounts should not keep sockets.

variants.name: Direct message injection
variants.payload: Send a message addressed to a foreign room/user through the socket.
variants.expect: Rejected per-message — relay re-checks the target.
variants.why: Send authorization is per message, not per socket.

checks.title: Backend integrations resist confused deputy
checks.why: Server-side integrations act with service authority on user input (URLs, ids, templates) — the deputy serves whoever steers it.
checks.validate: Integration actions carry the caller context (or narrow service scope) and cannot be steered to foreign objects or endpoints.

variants.name: Steer-to-foreign
variants.payload: Where an integration takes an object/id/url (fetch, render, import, notify), point it at a B object or internal endpoint.
variants.expect: Refused or strictly scoped — the deputy never acts beyond the caller rights.
variants.why: The server holds the keys; the user holds the wheel — both must matter.

variants.name: Callback/URL injection
variants.payload: Integration URLs (webhook target, fetch-url) pointing at internal ranges or your Collaborator.
variants.expect: Blocked (SSRF controls) and logged; outbound targets allowlisted.
variants.why: Deputy problems are often SSRF problems.

variants.name: Cross-tenant integration
variants.payload: Configure an integration in tenant-1 referencing tenant-2 resources.
variants.expect: Refused — integrations are tenant-bound like every other object.
variants.why: Integrations are objects with privileges.

checks.title: New and undocumented functions denied by default
checks.why: Routes absent from the policy inventory inherit whatever the framework defaults to — often authenticated-and-allowed.
checks.validate: Undocumented/newly deployed functions deny by default until policy is authored; framework defaults are deny.

variants.name: Inventory diff
variants.payload: Diff documented endpoints (OpenAPI, docs) against observed routes (proxy history, JS bundles); probe undocumented ones as a standard user.
variants.expect: Undocumented functions refuse standard users — or are documented gaps to report.
variants.why: The dark API is usually bigger than the bright one.

variants.name: Preview/dark-route probe
variants.payload: Request likely upcoming routes (versioned, feature-flagged paths seen in JS) as a standard user.
variants.expect: Denied without explicit policy; presence with access is a finding.
variants.why: Bundles leak the future; policy should already deny it.

variants.name: Framework default check
variants.payload: Probe a guaranteed-unmatched path shape that still routes (new verb on existing resource).
variants.expect: Falls into deny (403/404), not accidental allow.
variants.why: Routing tables are policies you did not write.

checks.title: Admin interfaces layered authorization
checks.why: Admin panels concentrate every dangerous function; single-layer checks (one role string) fail wide when wrong.
checks.validate: Administrative functions require layered checks: role + scope (tenant/org) + explicit permission, with step-up for destructive actions.

variants.name: Cross-scope admin
variants.payload: Tenant-1 admin account against tenant-2 admin functions (path or id swap).
variants.expect: Refused — admin of one is not admin of all.
variants.why: Scoped admins are the rule in multi-tenant products.

variants.name: Destructive step-up
variants.payload: Attempt destructive admin actions (delete tenant, reset user, rotate keys) with a plain admin session lacking step-up.
variants.expect: Requires re-auth/MFA confirmation per policy; refusal otherwise.
variants.why: Admin destruction deserves a second factor.

variants.name: Legacy admin paths
variants.payload: Enumerate documented-old admin paths (/admin, /manage, /internal, /backoffice) as regular and admin users.
variants.expect: Consistent layered enforcement across all admin surfaces — no softer twin.
variants.why: Old admin UIs outlive the policies that guarded new ones.

checks.title: Authorization consistent across API versions
checks.why: v2 fixes the authorization bug, v1 keeps it; deprecated mobile clients keep v1 alive for years.
checks.validate: Every live version (path, header, content-type, query variants) enforces the same authorization rules.

variants.name: Version matrix
variants.payload: Replay your best authorization probes against every version marker: /v1 vs /v2 paths, Accept headers, content types, and ?version=.
variants.expect: Same refusal on all live versions; document any version that lags.
variants.why: Enumerate versions first — they hide in headers too.

variants.name: Beta/preview flags
variants.payload: Access preview endpoints via beta headers/flags as a standard user.
variants.expect: Preview surfaces enforce current policy or deny.
variants.why: Betas ship authorization half-done.

variants.name: Sunset honesty
variants.payload: Check whether deprecated versions are scheduled, throttled, or logged.
variants.expect: Retirement plan exists for report completeness; open-ended v1 is risk to note.
variants.why: Versions without funerals never die.
